correctness.rationale: For categorical/direct K_m times K_n (m,n>=3) two vertices adjacent iff row and column both differ, so nonadjacent iff same row/column; diameter 2 and their common neighbors can be written explicitly. If max(m,n)>=4, iterating intervals from any same-row or same-column pair fills all grid cells via two unused opposite columns or two available opposite rows; hence every proper convex subset is a clique, exactly a partial permutation matrix. Count partial matchings as binom(m,k)binom(n,k)k! and subtract from (1+z)^(mn). In K_3 times K_3, same-row pair forces a four-cell cross; any maximal proper closure adds one of two corner diagonals to give one of six complements of full permutation matrices. Inclusion-exclusion on these six six-sets gives 6z^3+45z^4+90z^5+78z^6+36z^7+9z^8+z^9; hull number 3, six minima. Generic hull number 2, with m binom(n,2)+n binom(m,2) minima. Independently implemented diameter-two interval closure from adjacency and enumerated all subsets for (3,3),(3,4),(4,3), matching every coefficient. Remaining large instances rely on structural proof, not enumeration.
